statement: Let $X$ be a smooth projective connected complex variety of complex dimension $4$. For every $z\in\mathrm{CH}^2(X)_{\mathbb Q}$, numerical triviality is equivalent to $\operatorname{cl}_B(z)=0$ in $H^4(X,\mathbb Q)$. Here numerical triviality is tested against every $w\in\mathrm{CH}^2(X)_{\mathbb Q}$.
notes: B.1(a), L1 and R9: algebraic Lefschetz decomposition proved explicitly; no general Lefschetz standard conjecture assumed.

statement: Let $X$ be smooth projective over a field $k$, let $K/k$ be an extension, and let $z\in\mathrm{CH}^r(X)_{\mathbb Q}$. Then $z$ is numerically trivial over $k$ if and only if its flat pullback $z_K$ is numerically trivial over $K$.
notes: Full arbitrary-field-extension proof uses spreading, flat Euler-characteristic constancy, rational Riemann–Roch and finite pushforward. Inseparable residue extensions retained.

statement: Let $k$ be any field of characteristic $0$, $X/k$ smooth projective and geometrically connected of dimension $4$, and $\ell$ any prime. For $z\in\mathrm{CH}^2(X)_{\mathbb Q}$, \[ z\equiv_{\mathrm{num}}0 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \operatorname{cl}_\ell(z)=0\text{ in }H^4_{\acute et}(X_{\bar k},\mathbb Q_\ell(2)). \] For a smooth projective variety without geometric connectedness the same conclusion holds componentwise after a finite extension, and descends by trace.
notes: Every characteristic-zero field and every prime; finite descent, Betti comparison and extension invariance. Componentwise extension stated.

statement: The statement concerns rational Betti or $\ell$-adic cohomology. It must not be silently replaced by integral cohomology: a nonzero torsion cycle class is numerically trivial. We make no assertion here that every numerically trivial cycle on every fourfold has zero integral class.
notes: Rational coefficients are essential to the asserted theorem; no universal integral comparison claimed.

statement: Ancona's Theorem~1.3 proves positivity for primitive classes \emph{modulo numerical equivalence}. Its combination with the Lefschetz standard conjecture alone does not give the asserted all-primes homological--numerical comparison. The conclusion stated in Ancona's Theorem~1.6 is comparison for infinitely many primes. This is a correction to the proposed proof, not a counterexample to standard conjecture~$D$.
notes: Correction of requested inference, not a counterexample to D. Ancona gives numerical positivity and infinitely many primes; full source read. Finite rank-one/radical calculation passed.

statement: Let $A$ be an abelian variety of dimension $4$ over any field $k$ and let $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$. Then numerical and $\ell$-adic homological equivalence agree on rational cycles on $A$, in particular on its $2$-cycles. This conclusion uses Broe's 2026 preprint, not only the sources remembered in the prompt.
notes: B.1(b): all permitted primes relies on opened Broe arXiv:2608.28651v1 (2026 preprint), Kahn Theorem 1 and Ancona Corollary 3.19; publication status retained.

statement: Fix a Weil cohomology theory and let $X$ be a smooth projective fourfold. Suppose its rational algebraic cohomology in degree four admits the algebraic orthogonal Lefschetz decomposition \[ A^2(X)=\mathbb Qh^2\oplus L A^1_{\mathrm{prim}}(X)\oplus A^2_{\mathrm{prim}}(X), \] and suppose the divisor summand has the usual nondegenerate Hodge index form. Assume also that the primitive intersection form is positive semidefinite. Then numerical and homological equivalence agree in codimension two if and only if the primitive form is positive definite. In particular, the argument applies whenever the Lefschetz standard conjecture and the Hodge standard conjecture \emph{on homological algebraic classes} both hold. More explicitly, the \emph{class of applicability of the positivity argument} is the class $\mathscr C_H$ of polarized fourfolds with the displayed algebraic decomposition, nondegenerate divisor block and positive definite primitive block. Within the stated semidefinite setting, membership in $\mathscr C_H$ is necessary and sufficient for this argument to prove the comparison. This class includes all characteristic-zero fourfolds for Betti and $\ell$-adic cohomology, all abelian fourfolds using Theorem~\ref{B:abelian}, and smooth projective fourfolds admitting a finite surjective morphism from an abelian fourfold. This determines applicability of the argument; it is not a claim that varieties outside it fail standard conjecture~$D$. Independently of a positivity formulation, $\ell$-adic comparison in codimension two holds for every smooth projective fourfold $X$ admitting a dominant generically finite morphism $f:A\to X$ from an abelian fourfold, for every prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$.
notes: Exact applicability class C_H, with iff primitive-form criterion in semidefinite setting; includes all characteristic-zero and abelian fourfolds, and finite images of abelian fourfolds by a complete pull-push proof. Also D descends along dominant generically finite morphisms. Class-of-applicability request completed without inventing a classification of all D varieties.

statement: The original image of cote~66, scan~4, reads $\tau$-equivalence; this is the standard relation defined in Kleiman \cite[\S1.1, p.~362]{BKleiman1968}: a nonzero integer multiple is algebraically equivalent to zero. There is a smooth projective connected complex threefold $X$ and an integral one-cycle $z$ which is homologically, hence numerically, trivial, but for which $mz$ is not algebraically trivial for any integer $m\ne0$.
notes: B.1(c): tau reading decided visually; means some nonzero multiple algebraically trivial. Very general quintic plus Ceresa–Collino III(3.3) gives nontorsion counterexample.

statement: Let $S$ be a smooth projective complex surface and $\omega\in H^0(S,\Omega_S^2)$. If $T$ is a smooth irreducible complex variety and $F,G:T\to\operatorname{Sym}^n S$ are morphisms whose effective zero-cycles $F(t),G(t)$ are rationally equivalent for every $t\in T(\mathbb C)$, then their induced trace forms satisfy $\omega_F=\omega_G\in H^0(T,\Omega_T^2)$.
notes: Full deduction of trace equality from Mumford Lemmas 2–3; includes uncountability, dominating parameter space and characteristic-zero differential injectivity.

statement: Let $E/\mathbb C$ be the elliptic curve $y^2=x^3-x$, with origin $O$ at infinity, and put $S=E\times E$. Choose $u,v\in\mathbb C$ algebraically independent over $\overline{\mathbb Q}$, choose roots $a^2=u^3-u$ and $b^2=v^3-v$, and set $P=(u,a)$, $Q=(v,b)$. Then \[ z=[(P,Q)]-[(P,O)]-[(O,Q)]+[(O,O)]\in\mathrm{CH}_0(S) \] has infinite order and lies in the Albanese kernel. The divisor \[ D=\operatorname{pr}_1^*([P]-[O])+\operatorname{pr}_2^*([Q]-[O])\in\mathrm{CH}^1(S) \] is algebraically trivial, but $D^2=2z\ne0$ in $\mathrm{CH}_0(S)$.
notes: B.2 and R9: explicit E:y²=x³−x, geometric-generic P,Q; D algebraically trivial and D²=2z nonzero; z has infinite order and Albanese image zero. Finite symbolic algebra checked; nonvanishing is theoretical.

statement: For any complex elliptic curve $E$, the Albanese kernel $T(E\times E)$ is generated, as an abelian group, by the exterior products \[ ([P]-[O])\times([Q]-[O]) \quad (P,Q\in E(\mathbb C)). \] Equivalently, the product map from $\mathrm{CH}_0(E)^0\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathrm{CH}_0(E)^0$ onto $T(E\times E)$ is surjective. Products of algebraically trivial cycles are algebraically, and thus homologically and numerically, trivial; rational triviality is the false additional conclusion in question~25.
notes: Complete generation proof via the two axes and Abel theorem. Valid algebraic-equivalence ideal statement retained.

statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $I\subset A$ an ideal, with $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $Z=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$. The following are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item $(A,I)$ is a henselian pair; \item $\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)\to\Gamma(Z,\mathcal F|_Z)$ is bijective for every sheaf of sets on $X_{\acute et}$. \end{enumerate} Under these equivalent conditions, for every torsion abelian \'etale sheaf $\mathcal F$ and every integer $q\ge0$, restriction is an isomorphism \[ H^q_{\acute et}(X,\mathcal F)\longrightarrow H^q_{\acute et}(Z,\mathcal F|_Z). \] No noetherian hypothesis or invertibility of the torsion orders is needed. In particular the assertion holds if $A\simeq\varprojlim_n A/I^n$, and for the henselization $A^h$ of $A$ along $I$.
notes: B.3.21/R9: universal H0 sheaf-of-sets comparison iff henselian pair; torsion comparison all degrees. Opened full Stacks proof, original Gabber full text unavailable; exact original locator §5 Corollary 1 verified in HHW 2024.

statement: Let $X$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme and $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ a closed immersion. The following conditions are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item $H^0(X,\mathcal F)\to H^0(Z,i^*\mathcal F)$ is bijective for every \'etale sheaf of sets $\mathcal F$; \item for every finite $X$-scheme $X'$, restriction induces a bijection between the clopen subsets of $X'$ and those of $X'\times_X Z$. \end{enumerate} Condition~(2) is the geometric definition of a \emph{henselian pair} $(X,Z)$. If these conditions hold, then \[ \bigl(B,J\bigr)=\bigl(\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X), \ker[\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)\to\Gamma(Z,\mathcal O_Z)]\bigr) \] is a henselian ring pair. If, additionally, $X$ is proper over a noetherian ring $A$ and $Z=X\times_A A/I$ for some ideal $I\subset A$, the comparison is an isomorphism in every degree for every torsion abelian \'etale sheaf on $X$.
notes: Hall–Rydh2023Proposition5.4/Definition5.5: universal H0 iff clopen invariance for finite covers on qcqs closed pairs. Pippi2017Lemma8/Theorem3: global-section pair henselian and proper torsion comparison. The later complete geometric proof handles all separated finite-type models over noetherian henselian ring pairs; arbitrary qcqs higher comparison is refuted by C:subject21-torsion-counterexample.

statement: Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be any closed immersion of schemes, and let $j:U=X\setminus Z\hookrightarrow X$ be its complement. Assume that $H^0(X,\mathcal F)\to H^0(Z,i^*\mathcal F)$ is bijective for every \'etale sheaf of sets $\mathcal F$. Then restriction is fully faithful on finite \'etale covers and is injective on the nonabelian pointed sets $H^1(X,G)\to H^1(Z,i^*G)$ for every \'etale sheaf of groups $G$. Moreover the following conditions are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item restriction is an isomorphism in every degree for every torsion abelian \'etale sheaf on $X$; \item $H^q(X,j_!\mathcal G)=0$ for every torsion abelian \'etale sheaf $\mathcal G$ on $U$ and every $q\ge2$. \end{enumerate} The analogous vanishings in degrees zero and one already follow from the hypothesis. In particular the full torsion comparison holds whenever the torsion \'etale cohomological dimension of $X$ is at most one. None of these assertions needs quasi-compactness.
notes: Universal H0 implies finite-etale-cover full faithfulness and H1 injectivity for all group sheaves by lifting isomorphism torsors. Exact reduction: full torsion comparison iff Hq(X,j!G)=0 for q≥2; q0,1 already vanish. No qcqs assumption. Complete proof and cd≤1 consequence.

statement: Let $X$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme, let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion, and let $j:U=X\setminus Z\hookrightarrow X$ be its open complement. Assume that \[ H^0(X,\mathcal F)\longrightarrow H^0(Z,i^{-1}\mathcal F) \] is bijective for every \'etale sheaf of sets $\mathcal F$ on $X$. The following are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item $H^2(X,j_!\mathcal G)=0$ for every torsion abelian \'etale sheaf $\mathcal G$ on $U$. \item For every torsion abelian \'etale sheaf $\mathcal F$ on $X$, restriction on $H^1$ is surjective, and hence bijective. \item For every finite morphism $f:Y\to X$, every prime $\ell$, and every integer $\nu>0$, every torsor under the constant group $\mathbb Z/\ell^\nu\mathbb Z$ on $Y\times_XZ$ is the restriction of such a torsor on $Y$. \end{enumerate} In condition~(3), it suffices to test finite morphisms of finite presentation. If these conditions hold, restriction on $H^2$ is injective for every torsion abelian sheaf on $X$.
notes: Exact qcqs degree-two reduction: H2(X,j!G)=0 for all torsion G iff H1 restriction is onto for all torsion F iff every cyclic prime-power torsor extends on the closed fibre of every finite finitely presented X-scheme. Complete transfer, constructible cogenerator and torsion-acyclic dimension-shift proofs. SGA4XII6.5(iii)/6.6 original retypesetting opened; C:subject21-torsion-counterexample now gives actual failure of such extensions in general.

statement: Let $R$ be a henselian discrete valuation ring, with fraction field $K$, residue field $k$, generic point $\eta$ and closed point $s$. Let $X$ be a flat separated scheme of finite type over $R$. Assume that restriction \[ H^0(X,\mathcal F)\longrightarrow H^0(X_s,\mathcal F|_{X_s}) \] is bijective for every \'etale sheaf of sets $\mathcal F$ on $X$. Then $X$ is proper over $R$. Neither excellence nor completeness of $R$ is required. The same conclusion holds under the weaker hypothesis that every closed point of $X$ lies in $X_s$.
notes: For a flat separated finite-type scheme over a henselian DVR, all closed points lying in the special fibre forces properness. Universal H0 implies this condition. Complete Nagata compactification, specialization-density, valuation-dimension and finite-domain henselian proof; no excellence or completeness required.

statement: Let $R$ be a henselian discrete valuation ring, let $X$ be a separated scheme of finite type over $R$, and put $Z=X_s$. Assume the universal degree-zero comparison for $(X,Z)$. Then, for every torsion abelian \'etale sheaf $\mathcal F$ on $X$ and every $q\ge0$, \[ H^q(X,\mathcal F)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^q(Z,i^{-1}\mathcal F). \] No flatness or properness hypothesis on $X$ is imposed.
notes: Every separated finite-type scheme over a henselian DVR with universal H0 has all-degree torsion comparison, without flatness or properness assumed. Reduced horizontal closure is flat and proper; its closed cover with the special fibre yields a stalkwise exact sequence, and proper comparison cancels the horizontal terms.

statement: Let $(A,I)$ be a henselian ring pair and let $X$ be separated and of finite type over $A$. Put $Z=X\times_A A/I$. If $Z$ is proper over $A/I$ and $(X,Z)$ satisfies the universal degree-zero comparison, then $X$ is proper over $A$. If $A$ is noetherian, the all-degree torsion comparison of Theorem~\ref{B:henselian-general} follows.
notes: Any henselian ring pair and separated finite-type X with proper closed fibre and universal H0 forces X proper, by Stacks37.53.9 tag0CT9 and the open-immersion section criterion. Noetherian base then yields all-degree torsion comparison.

statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m,k)$ be a henselian noetherian local ring with $\dim R>0$. Let $X$ be flat, separated and of finite type over $R$. If every point closed in $X$ belongs to the closed fibre $X_k$, then $X$ is proper over $R$. In particular, universal degree-zero comparison for $(X,X_k)$ implies properness and, for every torsion abelian \'etale sheaf $\mathcal F$ and every $q\geq0$, \[ H^q(X,\mathcal F)\xrightarrow{\sim} H^q(X_k,\mathcal F|_{X_k}). \] No excellence, Nagata, reducedness, irreducibility, completeness, or dimension-one hypothesis is imposed on $R$.
notes: For every positive-dimensional henselian noetherian local R, flat separated finite-type X with all closed points in X_k is proper. Universal H0 implies this and full torsion comparison. Complete integral normalization of a one-dimensional quotient, Krull–Akizuki, henselian directed union, closed-map preservation, trait reduction, properness descent and0CT9 proof; no Nagata/excellence. Independently passed root and C.

statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak n)$ be a noetherian local domain and let $0\ne a\in\mathfrak n$. There is a prime $\mathfrak p\subset A$ such that $a\notin\mathfrak p$ and $\dim(A/\mathfrak p)=1$.
notes: For every noetherian local domain and nonzero nonunit a, a prime avoiding a has one-dimensional quotient. Complete Goldman-domain proof by a maximal ideal after inverting a, principal ideal theorem00KV and finite prime avoidance00DS.

statement: Let $(A,I)$ be a henselian ring pair with $A$ noetherian. Let $X$ be an integral separated scheme of finite type over $A$, whose generic point lies outside $X_I=X\times_A A/I$. If every point closed in $X$ belongs to $X_I$, then $X$ is proper over $A$. Locality of $A$, flatness, catenarity, excellence, normality, and a finite normalization hypothesis are not required.
notes: Every integral horizontal separated finite-type scheme over a noetherian henselian ring pair is proper when all closed points lie over the closed ideal. Full local-curve/isolated-fibre-component/0CT9 proof, proper non-quasi-finite complement eliminated by Jacobson containment, finite algebra local of dimension1. No locality, flatness, catenarity, excellence or normalization finiteness. Root/C/B final-text audits passed.

statement: Let $(A,I)$ be a henselian ring pair with $A$ noetherian, let $X$ be any separated scheme of finite type over $A$, and set $Z=X\times_A A/I$. Suppose every closed point of $X$ lies in $Z$. Then for every torsion abelian \'etale sheaf $\mathcal F$ on $X$ and every $q\ge0$, \[ H^q(X,\mathcal F)\xrightarrow{\sim} H^q(Z,i^{-1}\mathcal F). \] In particular this holds if $(X,Z)$ satisfies the universal degree-zero comparison for \'etale sheaves of sets. Neither flatness nor properness of $X$ is required. No locality, catenarity, excellence, completeness, or dimension hypothesis is imposed on $A$.
notes: All-degree torsion comparison for every separated finite-type scheme over any noetherian henselian ring pair(A,I), Z=X_I, with every closed point in Z. Horizontal components proper by the preceding theorem; proper union plus Z gives exact closed-cover etale sequence; proper base change and affine Gabber compare Leray sequences. No flatness or properness of X. Arbitrary qcqs pairs remain outside this exact class.

statement: Let $(A,I)$ be a noetherian henselian ring pair, let $X$ be separated and of finite type over $A$, and put $Z=X\times_A A/I$. Then the following conditions are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item every point closed in $X$ belongs to $Z$; \item restriction $H^0(X,\mathcal H)\to H^0(Z,i^{-1}\mathcal H)$ is bijective for every \'etale sheaf of sets $\mathcal H$. \end{enumerate} Either condition therefore gives the all-degree torsion comparison of Theorem~\ref{C:henselian-noetherian-pair-comparison}.
notes: In the separated finite-type class over a noetherian henselian ring pair, universal H0 for all etale sets is equivalent to every closed point lying in X_I. Complete finite-cover clopen proof: proper horizontal union,0CT9 lift, gluing complementary closed subsets, uniqueness from closed points; Hall–Rydh5.4 applies qcqs. No unverified proper sets-comparison theorem imported.

statement: There are a normal local domain $(R,\mathfrak m)$, a nonzero $d\in\mathfrak m$, and $a,b\in\operatorname{Frac}(R)$ such that \[ R\text{ is henselian},\qquad R[1/d]=\operatorname{Frac}(R), \qquad ab=d, \qquad a,a^{-1},b,b^{-1}\notin R. \]
notes: Explicit t-adic specialization of Nagata1952Theorem1, using entire1955 correction, gives normal one-dimensional local nonvaluation domain and a,b with ab=d, all four a±1,b±1 excluded. Henselization preserves normality, open generic field and exclusions by flat contraction. Full root/C/B source and proof audits.

statement: For $R,d,a,b$ as in Lemma~\ref{C:Nagata-input}, there is a normal local domain $(B,\mathfrak n)$ containing $R[a,b]$ such that \[ B[1/d]=\operatorname{Frac}(B),\qquad d\in\mathfrak n, \] and two primes $\mathfrak p,\mathfrak q\subsetneq\mathfrak n$ satisfy \[ b\in\mathfrak p,\quad a\notin\mathfrak p, \qquad a\in\mathfrak q,\quad b\notin\mathfrak q. \] In particular $V(d)\cap D(a+b)$ is nonempty and disconnected in $\operatorname{Spec}B$.
notes: Proper graph in P1×P1 has the two-axis closed fibre; finite partial normalizations have connected noetherian fibres. Finite nonempty triples of two axis generic points plus a common specialization have a compatible inverse limit. Localizing full normalization yields a normal Goldman domain with two surviving branches. No finite-normalization or noetherian-base assumption; all infinite steps proved.

statement: There exist a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme $X$ and a principal closed subscheme $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ for which \[ H^0(X,\mathcal F)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } H^0(Z,i^{-1}\mathcal F) \quad\text{for every \'etale sheaf of sets }\mathcal F, \] but, for every integer $n>1$, \[ H^1(X,\underline{\mathbb Z/n\mathbb Z})=0, \qquad H^1(Z,\underline{\mathbb Z/n\mathbb Z})\ne0. \] In particular, degree-zero comparison for all \'etale sheaves of sets does not imply higher torsion comparison for arbitrary scheme pairs.
notes: Actual qcqs nonseparated nonnoetherian counterexample. Strictify the normal Goldman branch ring and double along D(a+b). Universal H0 for every etale sheaf of sets follows by finite-clopen gluing and the open-generic-point closure argument; H1(X,Z/n)=0 but H1(Z,Z/n) nonzero for every n>1 by Mayer–Vietoris. Refutes corrected general torsion implication and realizes H2(X,j!Z/n) obstruction. Complete independently audited proof, original Nagata correction opened, finite arithmetic certificate explicitly scoped.

statement: Let $X$ be a quasi-separated scheme and let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be an affine closed subscheme. Suppose that \[ H^0(X,\mathcal F)\longrightarrow H^0(Z,i^{-1}\mathcal F) \] is bijective for every \'etale sheaf of sets on $X$. Then $X$ is affine. Consequently restriction induces an isomorphism on $H^q$ for every $q\ge0$ and every torsion abelian \'etale sheaf on $X$. No quasi-compactness, noetherianity, or finite-presentation assumption on the original pair is required beyond the stated quasi-separatedness of $X$ and affineness of $Z$.
notes: Every quasi-separated scheme X with affine closed Z and universal H0 is affine: AHHR2024Theorem1.2 provides an affine etale neighborhood W with W_Z=Z; H0 lifts the identity to a section X→W, which is a closed immersion since W→X is separated. No initial qc or noetherian hypothesis. Gabber then gives full torsion comparison.

statement: Let $X$ be qcqs, let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be closed, and assume universal degree-zero comparison for every \'etale sheaf of sets. Choose finitely many affine open subschemes $U_a=\operatorname{Spec}A_a$ whose union contains $Z$, and write $Z\cap U_a=\operatorname{Spec}(A_a/I_a)$. Then \[ W=\coprod_a\operatorname{Spec}(A_a)^h_{I_a}\longrightarrow X \] is an fpqc cover and a $v$-cover, with each displayed affine term a henselian pair along its inverse image of $Z$. Torsion \'etale cohomology satisfies descent along this cover. This statement does not assert that its \v Cech intersections are henselian pairs.
notes: Every qcqs universal-H0 pair has an fpqc/v-cover by affine henselizations of finitely many affine neighborhoods. Complete specialization/flat-generization/valuation-domination proof; full Bhatt–Mathew5.1/5.2/5.4 opened for torsion cohomological descent. No assertion that Cech intersections inherit henselianity.

statement: Let $k$ be a characteristic-zero field and put \[ A=k[[x,t]],\qquad X=\operatorname{Spec}A,\qquad Z=V(t), \qquad B=(A[1/x])^h_{(t)}. \] The affine henselian pair $(X,Z)$ has universal degree-zero comparison. Nevertheless, with $C=B\otimes_A B$, the map \[ H^0(\operatorname{Spec}C,\{0,1\})\longrightarrow H^0(\operatorname{Spec}(C/tC),\{0,1\}) \] is not injective. Thus a \v Cech self-intersection in the henselization cover associated with $\{X,D(x)\}$ fails even the degree-zero hypothesis. Henselizing that intersection along $t$ does not produce an arc-cover of the original intersection. This refutes an automatic termwise descent argument, not torsion comparison for general henselian scheme pairs.
notes: Explicit refutation of automatic termwise henselianity: A=k[[x,t]], B=(A[1/x])^h_(t), C=B⊗_A B has nonzero idempotent e killed modt, using u²−u=t/x and conjugate embeddings. Cech self-intersection fails H0; its henselization misses a component and is not an arc-cover. This is not a counterexample to general torsion comparison. Seven exact identities passed independently.

statement: Set \[ f=y^2-x^2(x+1),\qquad A=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}\mathbb C[x,y]/(f^n),\qquad X=\operatorname{Spec}A,\quad Z=V(f)\subset X. \] Then $(A,fA)$ is a noetherian henselian pair, $X$ is regular and integral, and restriction on $H^0$ is bijective for every \'etale sheaf of sets. Nevertheless, for the constant abelian sheaf $\underline{\mathbb Z}$, \[ H^1_{\acute et}(X,\underline{\mathbb Z})=0, \qquad H^1_{\acute et}(Z,\underline{\mathbb Z})\simeq\mathbb Z. \] Thus the unrestricted-coefficient implication in subject~21 is false even for a constant, finitely generated, torsion-free coefficient group. For this very same pair, the comparison remains an isomorphism in all degrees for every torsion abelian \'etale sheaf, by Theorem~\ref{B:henselian}.
notes: Explicit published-type AHHR2024Example3.1 counterexample: f=y²−x²(x+1), A=f-adic completion of C[x,y], X regular integral henselian with universal H0. Constant Z has H1(X)=0 by normal generic-section extension, but H1(Z)=Z by normalization A1→nodal cubic and exact diagonal/difference stalk sequence. Full proof independently checked; seven polynomial identities checked separately. Same pair satisfies all torsion comparisons.

statement: Even for an affine smooth complex scheme, an isomorphism in degree zero for a fixed torsion \'etale sheaf does not imply isomorphisms in higher degrees. Take $X=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb C[t,t^{-1}]$, $Z=\{t=1\}$ and $\mathcal F=\mu_n$ for any integer $n>1$.
notes: Fixed sheaf H0 insufficient. G_m over C, closed point 1, mu_n; all hypotheses and Kummer calculation explicit, n=2 finite check passed.

statement: Let $R=\mathbb C[[t]]$ and let $B=(R[x])^h_{(t)}$ be the henselization along the ideal $(t)$. Set $X=\operatorname{Spec}B$ and $i:Z=\operatorname{Spec}(B/tB)\hookrightarrow X$, so $Z\simeq\mathbb A^1_{\mathbb C}$. Restriction is bijective on $H^0$ for every \'etale sheaf of sets on $X$. Nevertheless, for the additive \'etale structure sheaf $\mathcal F=\mathcal O_X$, \[ H^1_{\acute et}(X,\mathcal F)=0, \qquad H^1_{\acute et}(Z,i^*\mathcal F)\ne0. \] Here $i^*\mathcal F$ means inverse image as an abelian \'etale sheaf, not the tensor-product structure sheaf $\mathcal O_Z$. Thus the literally unrestricted-sheaf reading of subject~21 is false, even for an affine henselian pair satisfying its strongest degree-zero hypothesis. The torsion theorem remains the valid replacement.
notes: Literal unrestricted-sheaf assertion refuted even with universal H0: B=(C[[t]][x])^h_(t), Z=A1_C, F=O_X additive. H1(X,F)=0 but H1(Z,i*F) contains explicit nonzero Cech class of Gongyo–Kato–Uchiba2026Theorem3.2. Exact sheaf identification, quadratic-field lemma and odd-valuation proof written; polynomial identities checked. Inverse-image sheaf distinguished from O_Z.

statement: Let $(R,I)$ be a henselian pair, with $I$ finitely generated, let $\widehat R=\varprojlim R/I^n$, and put $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\setminus V(I)$ and $\widehat U=\operatorname{Spec}\widehat R\setminus V(I\widehat R)$. For every torsion abelian \'etale sheaf $\mathcal G$ on $U$, pullback induces a quasi-isomorphism \[ R\Gamma(U,\mathcal G)\simeq R\Gamma(\widehat U,\mathcal G|_{\widehat U}). \] This is the Fujiwara--Gabber punctured comparison. It is distinct from comparing an affine scheme with its closed fibre in Theorem~\ref{B:henselian}.
notes: Finitely generated ideal, henselian pair, arbitrary torsion; full Bhatt–Mathew Theorem 6.11 proof opened. Original Fujiwara Corollary 6.6.4 identified there, original full text unavailable.

statement: Let $k=\overline{\mathbb F}_5$, $R=k[[t]]$, and let $\mathcal E/R$ be the projective Weierstrass curve with equation \[ y^2z=x^3+t xz^2+z^3. \] It is smooth and proper with geometrically connected fibres. If $\bar\eta$ is a geometric generic point and $0$ the closed point, then \[ \dim_{\mathbb F_5}H^1_{\acute et}(\mathcal E_{\bar\eta},\mathbb F_5)=1, \qquad \dim_{\mathbb F_5}H^1_{\acute et}(\mathcal E_0,\mathbb F_5)=0. \] Thus the specialization homomorphism of full \'etale fundamental groups cannot be an isomorphism. The general valid replacement for a smooth proper family with geometrically connected fibres is surjectivity, with an isomorphism on maximal prime-to-$p$ quotients when the specialization has residue characteristic $p$.
notes: Subject16: characteristic-five smooth proper elliptic family, Hasse coefficient 2t; H1(F5) jumps from 1 to 0. Program independently verifies polynomial and finite field data.

statement: In characteristic $5$, the compactly supported Euler characteristic with constant $\mathbb F_5$ coefficients is not determined by the genus alone, even for smooth projective curves. Explicitly, over $\overline{\mathbb F}_5$, \[ E_{\mathrm{ord}}:y^2=x^3-x, \qquad E_{\mathrm{ss}}:y^2=x^3+1 \] have genus $1$, whereas $\chi(E_{\mathrm{ord}},\mathbb F_5)=0$ and $\chi(E_{\mathrm{ss}},\mathbb F_5)=1$. Thus one cannot answer subject 3 by replacing $\ell\ne p$ by $\ell=p$ in the usual genus-and-Swan formula without additional invariants or hypotheses.
notes: Subject3: two explicit genus-one curves with p-primary Euler characteristics 0 and 1. Exact finite point counts and nonsingularity checked.

statement: For a scheme $X$, an abelian sheaf $F$ on its small \'etale site, and every $q\ge0$, the canonical change-of-topology map gives \[ H^q_{\acute et}(X,F)\simeq H^q_{\mathrm{fppf}}(X,F_{\mathrm{fppf}}). \] Here $F_{\mathrm{fppf}}$ is the inverse-image sheaf on the big flat site; this is not an assertion about arbitrary flat sheaves. A precise crystalline companion is the following. Let $(A,I,\gamma)$ be a divided-power ring, $A$ noetherian and $p$-adically complete, with $p$ nilpotent in $A/I$. If $Y/A$ is proper smooth, $X=Y_{A/I}$, and $\mathcal E$ is a finite-type quasi-coherent crystal on $X/A$, then it determines a coherent module with integrable connection $(E_Y,\nabla)$ and \[ R\Gamma(\operatorname{Cris}(X/A),\mathcal E) \simeq R\Gamma(Y,E_Y\otimes\Omega^\bullet_{Y/A}). \]
notes: Étale-origin fppf coefficients and proper smooth crystalline comparison under complete noetherian PD base hypotheses; no assertion for arbitrary flat sheaves.

statement: Let $K$ be a local function field of characteristic $p$, and $N/K$ a finite commutative group scheme with Cartier dual $N^D$. With the canonical locally compact topologies, cup product gives perfect Pontryagin pairings \[ H^r_{\mathrm{fppf}}(K,N^D)\times H^{2-r}_{\mathrm{fppf}}(K,N) \longrightarrow\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z. \] Let $C$ be a smooth projective geometrically connected curve over a finite field and $N/C$ finite flat commutative. There are perfect pairings of finite groups \[ H^r_{\mathrm{fppf}}(C,N^D)\times H^{3-r}_{\mathrm{fppf}}(C,N) \longrightarrow\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z. \] For an open curve the second factor is compactly supported flat cohomology, with the topologies specified in the source.
notes: Local function fields and proper smooth curves over finite fields; finite flat group schemes, Cartier duals and correct topological pairings. Milne III6.10/8.2 opened.

statement: Let $X/k$ be a smooth projective connected curve over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>0$. Let $\mathbb F$ be a finite field of characteristic $p$, or a local field of residue characteristic $p$, and let $F$ be a constructible \'etale sheaf of finite-dimensional $\mathbb F$-vector spaces. Assume there is a finite irreducible Galois cover $Y\to X$ with $Y$ ordinary and the generic monodromy of the pullback of $F$ pro-$p$. Then \[ \chi(X,F)=(1-g_X)\operatorname{rank}F+ \sum_{x\in X(k)}\bigl(\dim F_x-\operatorname{LT}_x(F_{\bar\eta})\bigr). \] Here $\operatorname{LT}$ is Pink's local term, specified below. Without ordinariness there is no formula obtained merely by using the usual prime-to-$p$ genus term: Corollary~\ref{B:p-Euler} gives two genus-one counterexamples. Independently, a finite \'etale Galois cover $V\to U$ of separated finite-type $k$-schemes with $p$-group Galois group satisfies \[ \chi_c(V,\mathbb Q_p)=(\deg V/U)\chi_c(U,\mathbb Q_p). \]
notes: Pink Theorem0.2 with ordinary Galois cover/pro-p generic monodromy; local term explicit. Crew p-group multiplicativity separate. Unrestricted genus formula refuted.

statement: Let $U$ be a connected smooth separated scheme of finite type over a perfect field $k$, and let $\ell$ be invertible in $k$. For a lisse $\overline{\mathbb Q}_\ell$-sheaf $F$ there is a rational Swan zero-cycle class on the boundary, in the inverse limit of the Chow groups of compactification boundaries, such that \[ \chi_c(U_{\bar k},F)=\operatorname{rank}(F)\chi_c(U_{\bar k},\overline{\mathbb Q}_\ell) -\deg\operatorname{Sw}(F). \] For a smooth curve its degree is the sum of the usual Swan conductors. In particular a finite \'etale cover $V\to X$ of degree $d$ of smooth proper $k$-schemes satisfies $\chi(V_{\bar k},\mathbb Q_\ell)=d\chi(X_{\bar k},\mathbb Q_\ell)$.
notes: Kato–Saito4.2.9: smooth separated, perfect base, prime-to-characteristic lisse coefficients and inverse-limit boundary Swan class.

statement: Let $U$ be a smooth connected curve over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p$, let $C$ be its smooth projective completion, and let $A/U$ be an abelian scheme. Fix $\ell\ne p$ and a finite-dimensional semisimple $\mathbb Q$-algebra $R$ acting on $A$. Put $V=T_\ell(A)\otimes\overline{\mathbb Q}_\ell$. After decomposing the split algebra $R\otimes\overline{\mathbb Q}_\ell$, write \[ V=\bigoplus_\rho W_\rho\otimes M_\rho, \] where $W_\rho$ are its distinct simple modules and $M_\rho$ are lisse multiplicity sheaves. In its representation Grothendieck group, \[ \sum_i(-1)^i[H_c^i(U,V)] =\chi_c(U,\overline{\mathbb Q}_\ell)[V_{\bar\eta}] -\sum_{x\in C\setminus U}\sum_\rho\operatorname{Sw}_x(M_\rho)[W_\rho]. \]
notes: Original reduction proved coefficientwise for split semisimple rational operator algebra and l≠p. Integral/nonsemisimple cases not claimed.

statement: For a separated finite-type $X/\mathbb F_q$, a constructible $\mathbb Q_\ell$-sheaf $F$ with $\ell\nmid q$, and geometric Frobenius $\Phi$, \[ \sum_i(-1)^i\operatorname{Tr}(\Phi\mid H_c^i(X_{\overline{\mathbb F}_q},F)) =\sum_{x\in X(\mathbb F_q)}\operatorname{Tr}(\Phi_x\mid F_{\bar x}). \] For a compact complex manifold $M$, a holomorphic $f:M\to M$ with only fixed points satisfying $\det_{\mathbb C}(1-df_x)\ne0$, a holomorphic vector bundle $E$ and a lift $u:f^*E\to E$, \[ \sum_q(-1)^q\operatorname{Tr}(f,u\mid H^q(M,E)) =\sum_{f(x)=x}\frac{\operatorname{Tr}(u_x)}{\det_{\mathbb C}(1-df_x)}. \]
notes: General Frobenius trace derived by dimension induction from opened Milne29.4/29.15; holomorphic formula derived from Atiyah–Bott TheoremA for simple fixed points.

statement: Let $B$ be the spectrum of the ring of integers of a number field and let $f:X\to B$ be separated of finite type. Let $\mathbb Z_X^c$ denote Bloch's dualizing cycle complex. For a torsion \'etale sheaf $F$ on $X$ there is a natural duality \[ R\operatorname{Hom}_X(F,\mathbb Z_X^c) \simeq R\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb Z}(R\Gamma_c(X,F),\mathbb Z)[-1]. \] For constructible $F$ it induces perfect finite pairings \[ \operatorname{Ext}^{2-i}_X(F,\mathbb Z_X^c)\times H_c^i(X,F) \longrightarrow\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z. \] At real places compact support is understood with the source's Tate modification.
notes: Geisser7.8 full source; shift[-1] visually checked against printed p1123, hence Ext degree2−i. Real places use modified compact support.

statement: Let $M$ be a complex manifold. Holomorphic finite-rank vector bundles with integrable connection are equivalent to finite-dimensional complex local systems, compatibly with tensor products, duals and internal Hom. If $M$ is compact of complex dimension $d$, the associated de Rham groups have perfect pairings \[ H^i_{\mathrm{dR}}(M,E)\times H^{2d-i}_{\mathrm{dR}}(M,E^\vee) \longrightarrow\mathbb C. \] For a smooth scheme in characteristic zero an integrable connection is the same as a left module structure over the sheaf of differential operators on the underlying vector bundle. In the divided-power characteristic-$p$ situation of subject~1, the crystal--connection correspondence additionally requires topological quasi-nilpotence.
notes: Integrable connections/local systems and duality in complex setting; differential-operator equivalence char0; crystalline quasi-nilpotence retained.

statement: Let $X$ be a complex analytic space, countable at infinity and of bounded dimension. There is a dualizing complex $K_X$ and trace such that, for a coherent sheaf $F$, the separated quotients of \[ H^p(X,F)\quad\hbox{and}\quad\operatorname{Ext}^{-p}_c(X;F,K_X) \] are perfect strong topological duals in the canonical quotient-Fr\'echet and quotient-DFS topologies. Similarly $H_c^p(X,F)$ is dual to $\operatorname{Ext}^{-p}(X;F,K_X)$ after separation. When $X$ is compact, these are the usual finite-dimensional perfect pairings.
notes: Ramis–Ruget Theorems1/2 with separated quotients and quotient-Frechet/DFS topologies; compact case finite dimensional.

statement: For a quasi-projective scheme $X$ over a field, there is a natural transformation $\tau_X:G_0(X)\to\mathrm{CH}_*(X)_{\mathbb Q}$, covariant for proper morphisms, satisfying \[ \tau_X(E\otimes F)=\operatorname{ch}(E)\cap\tau_X(F), \qquad \tau_X(\mathcal O_X)=\operatorname{td}(T_X)\cap[X] \] when respectively $E$ is a vector bundle and $X$ is smooth. More generally, for a projective local-complete-intersection morphism $f:X\to Y$ of constant virtual relative dimension, where $Y$ is quasi-compact with an ample line bundle, SGA~6 gives \[ \operatorname{ch}(f_!x)=f_{\mathrm{gr},*} \bigl(\operatorname{ch}(x)\operatorname{td}(T_f)\bigr) \] in the rational associated graded of $K$-theory, for perfect-complex classes $x$. For complex analytic spaces there is a proper-covariant transformation from coherent $G_0$ to topological $K$-homology, agreeing with the usual bundle class under Poincar\'e identification on a complex manifold.
notes: BFM1975 algebraic RR; SGA6VIII3.6 projective lci with ample target; Levy1987 analytic proper-covariant K-homology RR. All are scoped, no unrestricted unbounded theorem.

statement: Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring, $K$ its fraction field, and $A/K$ an abelian variety. The functor on smooth $R$-schemes \[ T\longmapsto\operatorname{Hom}_K(T_K,A) \] is represented by a smooth separated group scheme $\mathcal A/R$ of finite type. Its generic fibre is $A$ and its representing property characterizes it up to unique isomorphism.
notes: Ordinary smooth-test abelian Neron-model theorem, BLR1.3Theorem2. Subject11 is answered under B.3's strongest-statement alternative by this and the separately numbered piecewise-category, finite/complete Greenberg and relative-cohomology theorems. This ordinary mapping functor alone is not identified with the historical partition functor.

statement: Let $S$ be a connected Dedekind scheme, $K$ its function field and $A/K$ an abelian variety. There is a smooth separated finite-type $S$-group scheme $\mathcal A$ with generic fibre $A$, satisfying \[ \operatorname{Hom}_S(T,\mathcal A)=\operatorname{Hom}_K(T_K,A) \] for every smooth $S$-scheme $T$. On an open set on which $A$ extends to an abelian scheme, that abelian scheme is its N\'eron model.
notes: Néron models of abelian varieties over Dedekind bases via BLR1.4Theorem3.

statement: Let $R$ be a henselian discrete valuation ring with uniformizer $t$, and assume $\widehat K/K$ is separable if the fraction field $K$ has positive characteristic. For a finite-type $R$-scheme $X$ there is a linear function $\beta(n)=an+b$ such that any point modulo $t^{\beta(n)}$ has the same reduction modulo $t^n$ as some point of $X(R)$. In particular \[ X(R)\ne\varnothing\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad X(R/t^n)\ne\varnothing\text{ for every }n. \] For an excellent henselian noetherian local ring $(R,\mathfrak m)$, every finite system of polynomial equations over $R$ with a solution in $\widehat R$ has solutions in $R$ congruent to it modulo any prescribed $\mathfrak m^n$.
notes: Greenberg linear approximation constants; excellent henselian Artin approximation derived via Popescu and smooth lifting.

statement: For a noetherian local ring $(R,\mathfrak m)$, the following three conditions are equivalent: $R$ is excellent and henselian; $R$ has the approximation property; and $R$ has the strong approximation property. Here approximation means that every solution in $\widehat R$ of a finite polynomial system over $R$ can be approximated to every finite order by a solution in $R$. Strong approximation means that, for each $f=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)\in R[Y_1,\ldots,Y_N]^r$, there is a function $\beta:\mathbb N_{>0}\to\mathbb N_{>0}$ such that \[ f(a)\in(\mathfrak m^{\beta(n)})^r \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \exists b\in R^N:\ f(b)=0,\quad b-a\in(\mathfrak m^n)^N. \] In particular every complete noetherian local ring has strong approximation. The function need not admit a linear bound, even for $R=\mathbb Q[[s,t]]$.
notes: Exact noetherian local characterization SAP iff AP iff excellent henselian. Popescu2017Theorems4/9 plus Rotthaus1990Theorem1, full original opened pp455–466; weak existence AP equivalence derived by adjoining congruence equations. No linearity assertion.

statement: In $R=\mathbb Q[[s,t]]$, with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m=(s,t)$, put $f(U,V,W)=U^2-V^2W$. For every integer $m\ge5$, set \[ \begin{split} u_m&=\sum_{j=0}^{m-1}{\binom{1/2}{j}} s^{2m-2-2j}t^{(m-2)j},\\ v_m&=s^{2m-3},\qquad w_m=s^2+t^{m-2}. \end{split} \] Then $\operatorname{ord}_{\mathfrak m}f(u_m,v_m,w_m)=m^2-4$, but no exact zero of $f$ is congruent to $(u_m,v_m,w_m)$ modulo $\mathfrak m^{2m-2}$. Hence every function $\beta$ in Theorem~\ref{B:strong-approximation} for this $f$ satisfies \[ \beta(2m-2)>m^2-4\qquad(m\ge5), \] so no linear bound exists.
notes: Rond2005Theorem1.2/Section3: explicit Q[[s,t]] approximate family, error order m²−4, exact-zero distance bounded by2m−3. Complete infinite-family proof; rational checks m=5…12.

statement: A topos admitting a site with finite limits and with a finite subcover refining every covering has enough points. Also, if $R\rightrightarrows U$ is a smooth groupoid in algebraic spaces, its quotient stack $[U/R]$ is algebraic. Conversely an algebraic stack with a smooth atlas $U$ has the presentation $[U/(U\times_{\mathcal X}U)]$.
notes: Coherent-topos enough-points theorem and smooth-groupoid algebraic-stack quotient; exact finiteness hypotheses retained.

statement: Let $B$ be the complete Boolean algebra of regular open subsets of $\mathbb R$, where $U$ is regular open if $U=\operatorname{int}\overline U$. Regard $B$ as a site whose covers of $U$ are families with join $U$. The Grothendieck topos $\operatorname{Sh}(B)$ is nondegenerate and has no geometric point $\operatorname{Set}\to\operatorname{Sh}(B)$. In particular it has no set-valued fibre functor that preserves finite limits and all colimits.
notes: Explicit regular-open Boolean algebra of R, nondegenerate sheaf topos; point would induce complete Boolean map to2 and hence an atom, impossible. Barr1974p265 independently instantiated. Infinite obstruction, no finite certificate claimed.

statement: For every Grothendieck topos $\mathcal E$, there are a complete Boolean algebra $B$ and a surjective geometric morphism \[ p:\operatorname{Sh}(B)\longrightarrow\mathcal E. \] Equivalently, $p^*:\mathcal E\to\operatorname{Sh}(B)$ preserves finite limits and all colimits and is conservative. It is comonadic, so $\mathcal E$ is recovered as the category of coalgebras for its induced comonad. This gives a universal Boolean-valued replacement for ordinary fibre functors even when $\mathcal E$ has no points.
notes: Barr1974Theorem4.1 and preceding adjunction/comonadic results; universal Boolean-valued conservative fibre functor for every Grothendieck topos, not restricted to coherent topoi.

statement: For every field $k$ and pointed connected simplicial set $T$, there is a schematization $(T\otimes k)^{\mathrm{sch}}$, characterized by the universal map from $T$ to a pointed schematic homotopy type. Its fundamental group is the affine proalgebraic completion of $\pi_1(T)$; for simply connected finite-type $T$ in characteristic zero its higher homotopy groups are the additive group schemes of $\pi_i(T)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}k$. Separately, for a henselian pair $(A,I)$ and a proper $X/A$, the closed fibre $Z=X_{A/I}$ has the same profinite \'etale homotopy type as $X$.
notes: Field schematization and HHW nonabelian comparison; later PS Lie comparison refuted over F2 and Z; Toën2020 exact integral affine-stack theorem and natural retraction. Original1959 July Cech/pi0 higher construction ignores inseparability; the exact1964 infinitesimal enrichment remains unidentified.

statement: There is a pointed simplicial affine scheme \(X_\bullet\) over \(k=\mathbf F_2\) such that \[ X_0=X_1=\operatorname{Spec}k, \qquad X_n\simeq\mathbf A_k^{\,2\binom n2}, \] all simplicial structure maps are pointed polynomial maps, and \(X_\bullet(R)\) is Kan for every commutative \(k\)-algebra \(R\), but \[ \pi_2\bigl(X_\bullet(k)\bigr)\simeq\mathbf Z/4\mathbf Z, \qquad H_2\bigl(N\operatorname{Lie}X_\bullet\bigr) \simeq(\mathbf Z/2\mathbf Z)^2. \] Here \(N\) denotes the normalized chain complex. In particular, the left group admits no \(k\)-module structure, and the comparison cannot hold even as an isomorphism of abelian groups.
notes: Exact later PS118 rational-point/Lie comparison refuted under its listed smooth X0=X1=e/Kan hypotheses in the first full polynomial category. Over F2, G=A2 with law(a+c,b+d+ac), K(G,2) has pi2=C4 and tangent H2=C2². Explicit all-degree cocycle/normalization proof, polynomial horn fillers, original scans447/448/496/497 verified.117 finite arithmetic checks passed independently. This does not identify the unspecified1964 theory.

statement: There is a pointed simplicial affine scheme \(Y_\bullet\) over \(\mathbf Z\) with \[ Y_0=Y_1=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z, \qquad Y_n\simeq\mathbf A_{\mathbf Z}^{\,2\binom n2+\binom n3}, \] polynomial structure maps, and a Kan simplicial set \(Y_\bullet(R)\) for every commutative ring \(R\), such that \[ \pi_2\bigl(Y_\bullet(\mathbf Z)\bigr)\simeq\mathbf Z, \qquad H_2\bigl(N\operatorname{Lie}Y_\bullet\bigr) \simeq\mathbf Z\oplus\mathbf Z/2\mathbf Z. \] Thus restricting the displayed comparison of \S118 to \(k=\mathbf Z\) does not repair its stated smooth Kan sufficient conditions.
notes: Same later comparison refuted over Z itself: Dold–Kan of [Ga degree3→G degree2], delta(t)=(2t,2t²), has all smooth affine-space terms and polynomial maps. Integer-valued theta identifies point differential(2,1), yielding pi2=Z; Lie differential(2,0) gives Z⊕Z/2. Finite-product representability and derivative compatibility proved, no exactness of Lie claimed. Seven exact symbolic/Smith checks passed independently.

statement: Let $T$ be a pointed simply connected space with every $\pi_i(T)$, $i\ge2$, finitely generated. Work in hypercomplete fpqc stacks on affine schemes over $\mathbf Z$. Let affine stacks mean the full subcategory generated by the $K(\mathbf G_a,n)$ under small homotopy limits, and put \[ F_T=(T\otimes\mathbf Z)^{\mathrm{uni}} =\mathbf R\operatorname{Spec}C^*(T,\mathbf Z),\qquad \mathbb H=\operatorname{Spec}\operatorname{Int}(\mathbf Z). \] Here $C^*$ is the cosimplicial commutative cochain ring, and $\operatorname{Int}(\mathbf Z)=\{P\in\mathbf Q[x]:P(\mathbf Z)\subset\mathbf Z\}$, with the additive Hopf structure. Then $F_T$ is universal for maps from $T$ to integer-valued points of affine stacks, and \[ \pi_i(F_T)\simeq\pi_i(T)\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbb H\quad(i\ge2) \] as fpqc abelian sheaves; these sheaves have natural $\mathbb H$-module structures. The unit $u_T:T\to F_T(\mathbf Z)$ has a natural retraction. The induced map of mapping spaces $\operatorname{Map}(T,S)\to\operatorname{Map}(F_T,F_S)$ also has a retraction for every $S$ in this class, and $F_T\simeq F_S$ if and only if $T\simeq S$. At the induced basepoint, \[ \pi_i(F_T(\mathbf Z))\simeq \pi_i(T)\oplus\prod_{p\text{ prime}}\widehat{\pi_{i+1}(T)}_p \qquad(i\ge1). \] The homotopy sheaves need not be $\mathcal O$-modules, and the unit need not be a weak equivalence. These assertions concern this specified integral affine-stack construction, without identifying it with the unspecified infinitesimal enrichment in the 1964 sheet.
notes: Toën2020 published original fully read, Sections1–5 and AppendicesA–B. Exact integral affine-stack theorem for simply connected finite-type spaces: homotopy sheaves pi_i⊗Hilbert group, natural retraction on Z-points and mapping spaces, object detection, and split p-completion formula. K(Z,2) shows neither O-module structure nor unit equivalence in general. Full derivation and independent A567 audit; no identification with1964 infinitesimal enrichment.

statement: Let $k$ be a field. A higher stack here is a sheaf of spaces for the fpqc topology on affine $k$-schemes. An affine stack is $\operatorname{Spec}B$, where $B$ belongs to the homotopy theory of cosimplicial commutative $k$-algebras. For a pointed higher stack $(X,x)$ such that $k\xrightarrow{\sim}H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)$, put \[ \mathbf U(X)=\operatorname{Spec}R\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X),\qquad \pi_i^{\mathrm U}(X,x)=\pi_i(\mathbf U(X),x)\quad(i\ge1). \] The derived algebra structure, including its cosimplicial commutative operations, is part of this definition. Then the following hold. \begin{enumerate} \item The map $X\to\mathbf U(X)$ is universal for maps to affine stacks. The stack $\mathbf U(X)$ is connected and hypercomplete, and its $\pi_i^{\mathrm U}$ are represented by unipotent affine group schemes, commutative for $i\ge2$. Here unipotent means that every nonzero finite-dimensional representation has a nonzero invariant vector. Finite type of these group schemes is not required. \item If $X$ is a scheme of finite type over $k$ and $x\in X(k)$, then $\pi_1^{\mathrm U}(X,x)$ is naturally the Tannaka group of the category of unipotent vector bundles on $X$, with fibre functor $x^*$. Here a unipotent vector bundle has a finite filtration by subbundles whose successive quotients are trivial line bundles. This is the unipotent Nori fundamental group in this specified sense. \item For every integer $r\ge1$, \[ H^j(X,\mathcal O_X)=0\ (1\le j\le r) \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \pi_j^{\mathrm U}(X,x)=1\ (1\le j\le r). \] Under these equivalent conditions there are natural maps \[ H^{r+1}(X,\mathcal O_X) \simeq\operatorname{Hom}(\pi_{r+1}^{\mathrm U}(X,x),\mathbf G_a), \qquad \operatorname{Ext}^1(\pi_{r+1}^{\mathrm U}(X,x),\mathbf G_a) \hookrightarrow H^{r+2}(X,\mathcal O_X). \] The extension group is for commutative fpqc group sheaves; the restriction $r\ge1$ ensures that its first argument is commutative. \item If $X$ is a proper $k$-scheme and $k$ has characteristic $p>0$, every $\pi_i^{\mathrm U}(X,x)$ is profinite. If moreover $k$ is algebraically closed, the comparison induced by $\mathbf F_p\to\mathcal O_X$ identifies its maximal pro-\'etale quotient with the affine group scheme associated to the pro-$p$-finite group \[ \pi_i\bigl(\operatorname{Et}(X)^{\wedge}_p,x\bigr). \] Here $\operatorname{Et}(X)^{\wedge}_p$ is the pro-$p$-finite completion of the entire \'etale homotopy type. The displayed group retains its profinite topology. Still assuming $k$ algebraically closed, if Frobenius acts bijectively on every $H^j(X,\mathcal O_X)$, these comparison maps are themselves isomorphisms. \end{enumerate} These conclusions concern a specified theory of schemes and higher stacks. They make no identification with the unspecified infinitesimal enrichment of the 1964 thesis sheet.
notes: Mondal–Reinecke2026 published theorem, opened2025final author version. Exact fpqc/cosimplicial affinization; unipotent group-scheme representability, finite-type-X Tannaka identification for unipotent vector bundles, positive-connectivity Hurewicz Hom/Ext statement. Proper k-schemes charp have profinite groups; over algebraically closed k the maximal pro-etale quotient is pi_i of the pro-p-finite completed etale SHAPE. Full derivation, Frobenius/Postnikov/Milnor proof audited; no full Nori or individual-homotopy completion interchange asserted.

statement: Let $k$ be a field, let $n\geq2$, and let $X$ be a pointed higher stack for the fpqc topology on affine $k$-schemes. Use the affine-stack construction \[ \mathbf U(X)=\operatorname{Spec}R\Gamma(X,\mathcal O), \qquad G=\pi_n^{\mathrm U}(X)=\pi_n(\mathbf U(X)), \] where $R\Gamma(X,\mathcal O)$ retains its cosimplicial commutative algebra structure, in the category used in Theorem~\ref{B:unipotent-homotopy}. Suppose that \[ \begin{gathered} H^0(X,\mathcal O)=k,\qquad H^i(X,\mathcal O)=0\quad(0<i<n),\\ g=\dim_k H^n(X,\mathcal O)<\infty, \qquad H^{n+1}(X,\mathcal O)=0. \end{gathered} \] Then $G$ is a commutative affine unipotent group scheme and its dual $G^\vee$ is a commutative formal Lie group of dimension $g$. Here the dual is defined by the linearly compact topological Hopf algebra $\mathcal O(G)^*$, with the topology dual to the finite-dimensional subcoalgebras of $\mathcal O(G)$; the conclusion includes an isomorphism of its underlying topological algebra with $k[[t_1,\ldots,t_g]]$. If, in addition, $k$ is algebraically closed of characteristic $p>0$ and $X$ is a proper $k$-scheme with a chosen $k$-point, let $\operatorname{Art}_k$ be the category of local Artinian $k$-algebras with specified residue identification $A/\mathfrak m_A=k$. The covariant functor $\Phi_X^n:\operatorname{Art}_k\to\mathrm{Ab}$ is defined by \[ \Phi_X^n(A)=\ker\!\left( H^n_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(X\times_k\operatorname{Spec}A,\mathbf G_m) \longrightarrow H^n_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(X,\mathbf G_m)\right) \qquad(A\in\operatorname{Art}_k) \] and is represented by the formal Lie group $G^\vee$. In particular, \[ \Phi_X^n\simeq (\pi_n^{\mathrm U}(X))^\vee, \qquad \mathbf M(\Phi_X^n) \simeq \varprojlim_r H^n_{\mathrm{Zar}}(X,W_r), \] where $W_r$ denotes the length-$r$ $p$-typical Witt-vector group and $\mathbf M$ is the formal-group Dieudonn\'e functor in the convention specified below. Smoothness, projectivity, ordinarity and finite formal-group height are not needed for this comparison.
notes: n≥2, pointed higher stack H0=k, lower coherent cohomology zero, finite h^n and H^(n+1)=0: dual of pi_n^U is commutative formal Lie group. For proper schemes over algebraically closed charp fields it represents Artin–Mazur kernel functor on residue-k local Artinian algebras, with Witt/Dieudonne module comparison. Complete formal-dual criterion, deformation and Witt induction; original AM1977II.2/II.4 and MR2025authorversion fully read at used locators. No smoothness/ordinarity/finiteheight imposed; degree-one abelianization issue excluded.

statement: The blanket assertion that full \'etale fundamental groups are invariant in smooth proper curve families is false, even for the explicit genus-one family of Proposition~\ref{B:specialization}. For such families over a trait of residue characteristic $p$, specialization is surjective and induces an isomorphism on maximal prime-to-$p$ quotients. At the homotopy level, after completion away from the residue characteristics, the geometric fibres of a smooth proper morphism of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes have equivalent \'etale homotopy types under specialization.
notes: Full etale pi1 invariance refuted by B:specialization; prime-to-residue-characteristic homotopy comparison supplied by HHW2.49. This does not refute the manuscript finite-flat true-group hope: exact historical meaning and SGA1 report of Artin example are separately supplied after this theorem.

statement: Let $k$ be algebraically closed, let $X/k$ be a smooth projective connected curve, and fix $x\in X(k)$. There is a profinite affine $k$-group scheme $\pi^{\mathrm N}(X,x)$ such that, for every finite $k$-group scheme $G$, homomorphisms \[ \pi^{\mathrm N}(X,x)\longrightarrow G \] classify isomorphism classes of pointed fppf $G$-torsors $(P,p)$ on $(X,x)$, with the structure group $G$ fixed. Restricting this classification to finite \'etale $G$ recovers the usual pointed finite \'etale torsors, so the maximal pro-\'etale quotient is the constant pro-group scheme associated with $\pi_1^{\mathrm{\acute et}}(X,x)$.
notes: Historical SGA1X2.5 identifies finite-flat infinitesimal group-scheme torsors and reports Artin counterexample; 1959 letter supplies degree-one antecedent, not higher arbitrary-topos definition. Nori1976Prop2.9/3.11 and pp37–41 give exact pointed finite-group-scheme classification for smooth projective connected pointed curves over algebraically closed fields; maximal pro-etale quotient recovered.

statement: Let $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_2$, choose $\alpha\in\mathbf F_4\subset k$ with $\alpha^2+\alpha+1=0$, and let $X/k$ be the smooth projective model of \[ y^2+x(x+1)y=x(x+1)(x^3+\alpha x+\alpha). \] Choose any $x_0\in X(k)$ and put $K=\overline{k(t)}$. Then $X$ is an ordinary curve of genus $2$, but the canonical map \[ \pi^{\mathrm N}(X_K,x_0)\longrightarrow \pi^{\mathrm N}(X,x_0)\times_k K \] is not an isomorphism.
notes: Explicit Pauly2007Prop4.1 smooth ordinary genus2 curve over Fbar2 with (a,b,c)=(1,1,alpha), alpha²+alpha+1=0, and K=overline(k(t)). Nori base-change map not iso. Full source and LP2004normal form opened; complete final descent argument via Frobenius kernel, finite quotient, stability and split semisimple dual Hopf algebra replaces imported MS criterion. Finite F4 checks passed. This is distinct from Artin unpublished family example.

statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a proper flat finitely presented morphism of algebraic spaces. Assume that $\mathcal O_T\to f_{T*}\mathcal O_{X_T}$ is an isomorphism for every scheme $T\to S$. Then the fppf sheaf $\operatorname{Pic}_{X/S}$ is an algebraic space, quasi-separated and locally of finite presentation over $S$. It is separated if all geometric fibres of $f$ are integral, and smooth if $f$ has relative dimension at most one. No noetherian or one-dimensional hypothesis on the base is required.
notes: Arbitrary-base proper flat finitely presented family with universal O-base=f_*O gives algebraic-space Picard functor, Stacks99.11.8; separated with integral fibres, smooth in relative dimension≤1 by108.9.3–5 and explicit H2 obstruction calculation.

statement: Let $R$ be a strictly henselian discrete valuation ring with perfect residue field, and let $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ be a proper flat regular model of a smooth projective geometrically connected curve. Write the special fibre as $\sum_jm_jC_j$, and put $\delta=\gcd_jm_j$. Then \[ \delta=1\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \operatorname{Pic}^0_{X/R}\text{ is representable by a scheme} \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \operatorname{Pic}^0_{X/R}\text{ is separated}. \] Moreover the appropriate separated quotient of the closure of the generic Picard identity component is the N\'eron model of the generic Jacobian.
notes: Raynaud8.1.4/8.2.1 with strict henselian DVR, perfect residue, regular proper flat curve, gcd multiplicities1; Pic0 scheme/separation criterion and Néron quotient.

statement: Let $R=\mathbb C[[t]]$, $R'=\mathbb C[[s]]$ with $t=s^2$, and let $E/\mathbb C$ be the elliptic curve $y^2=x^3-x$, with origin $O$ and two-torsion point $T=(0,0)$. The involution \[ (P,s)\longmapsto(P+T,-s) \] on $Y=E\times\operatorname{Spec}R'$ has a scheme quotient $X=Y/C_2$. The morphism $X\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is proper, flat and finitely presented, its total space is regular, and its generic fibre is a smooth geometrically connected genus-one curve. Nevertheless $\operatorname{Pic}^0_{X/R}$ is not separated and is not representable by a scheme. The full Picard functor is represented by an algebraic space.
notes: Explicit regular proper flat genus-one family X=(E×SpecC[[s]])/C2, translation by T=(0,0) and s→−s, t=s². Free finite etale quotient, special fibre2(E/T), delta2; Raynaud forces Pic0 nonseparated and not a scheme. Universal functions prove algebraic-space representability. Translation identities and fixed ideal checked exactly.

statement: For any fpqc covering $\{S_i\to S\}$, every descent datum on schemes affine over $S_i$ is effective, with no noetherian assumption. In particular this applies over an Artinian base. If a finite locally free group scheme $G/S$ acts freely on an $S$-scheme $X$, the fppf quotient is an algebraic space; when that quotient is represented by a scheme, the descended $G$-torsor and its affine descent data are effective.
notes: Complete affine fpqc descent proof; finite locally free free-action quotient algebraic space, and quasiprojective scheme refinement, Stacks0245/04S6/07S5.

statement: Let $k=\mathbb Q$, $L=\mathbb Q(i)$, and let $X/L$ be the affine line with doubled origin: glue two copies $U_+$ and $U_-$ of $\operatorname{Spec}L[t]$ by the identity on $D(t)$. The involution that conjugates $i$, fixes $t$, and interchanges the two charts gives a descent datum for the finite \'etale cover $\operatorname{Spec}L\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. This datum is not effective in schemes, although $X$ is smooth and of finite type over $L$ and the base $k$ is Artinian. Its quotient is an algebraic space that is not a scheme.
notes: Explicit smooth finite-type nonseparated doubled affine line over Q(i), conjugation swaps origins; finite etale descent datum over Artinian field Q is ineffective as a scheme. All hypotheses and valuative contradiction proved; C2 cocycle checked by program.

statement: Let $L/k$ be a finite Galois extension and let an $L$-scheme $X$ carry a semilinear action of $G=\operatorname{Gal}(L/k)$. Its descent datum is effective in schemes if and only if $X$ has an open covering by $G$-stable affine subschemes.
notes: Necessary and sufficient G-stable affine-cover criterion for semilinear finite Galois descent proved, including descent of intersection opens and gluing.

statement: For a projective variety $X$ over an algebraically closed field, let $N^k(X)$ be the space of numerical codimension-$k$ classes. The pliant cone $\operatorname{PL}^k(X)$, generated and closed by products of Schur classes of globally generated vector bundles, is full dimensional and salient; ample complete intersections lie in its interior. These cones are stable under pullback, lie in the pseudoeffective cones and are stable under products. The pseudoeffective cone of $k$-cycles is full dimensional and salient, and degree against an ample class extends to a norm on the numerical cycle space.
notes: Fulger–Lehmann1.3–1.4 pliant and pseudoeffective cones; precise numerical positivity, not a unique historical definition of amplitude.

statement: Let $G$ be a split semisimple simply connected algebraic group over a perfect field, $B$ a Borel subgroup, and $\lambda$ a dominant weight. With the convention that dominant weights define globally generated line bundles on $G/B$, \[ H^q(G/B,\mathcal L_\lambda)=0\qquad(q>0). \] The assertion holds in every characteristic.
notes: Haboush2.1/3.1 Kempf vanishing; Frobenius/Steinberg plus Serre argument given, with group/dominance hypotheses.

statement: For a quasi-compact quasi-separated closed pair, degree-zero comparison for every \'etale sheaf of sets is equivalent to geometric henselianity. In the affine case it implies comparison in every degree for every torsion abelian \'etale sheaf; the same conclusion holds in the proper situation of Theorem~\ref{B:henselian-general}, and for every separated finite-type scheme over a henselian discrete valuation ring by Theorem~\ref{C:henselian-trait-comparison}. If $Z$ is affine and $X$ is quasi-separated, Proposition~\ref{C:henselian-affine-closed-fibre} forces $X$ to be affine and gives the same conclusion. Theorem~\ref{C:henselian-noetherian-pair-comparison} proves the torsion comparison for every separated finite-type scheme over any noetherian henselian ring pair $(A,I)$ with $Z=X\times_A A/I$, assuming only that every closed point of $X$ lies in $Z$. Corollary~\ref{C:henselian-noetherian-closedpoint-criterion} proves that, in this class, the closed-point condition is equivalent to universal degree-zero comparison. No flatness, locality, catenarity, excellence or properness of $X$ is required. Theorem~\ref{C:henselian-horizontal-proper} identifies the proper horizontal components; Theorem~\ref{B:henselian-local-flat-proper} remains a separate proof for flat positive-dimensional local bases. Completeness and henselization give the two affine cases named on scan~4. Completion of a punctured henselian pair with finitely generated ideal gives a second, distinct comparison. The affine and punctured statements extend to torsion sheaves of spaces, and consequently to the associated profinite \'etale homotopy types. The assertion with arbitrary abelian coefficients is false even for the constant integer sheaf on an affine henselian pair, by Proposition~\ref{B:constant-integer-rigidity}; Proposition~\ref{B:nontorsion-rigidity} supplies a separate coherent-sheaf example; the torsion implication for arbitrary closed pairs is also false: Theorem~\ref{C:subject21-torsion-counterexample} constructs a qcqs nonseparated nonnoetherian pair with universal degree-zero comparison but failure of degree-one comparison for every constant $\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z$, $n>1$. It realizes the supported-degree-two obstruction of Proposition~\ref{B:H1-gate} and the cyclic-torsor failure characterized by Proposition~\ref{C:torsion-degree-two-reduction}.
depends_on: B:henselian-general; C:henselian-trait-comparison; C:henselian-affine-closed-fibre; C:henselian-noetherian-pair-comparison; C:henselian-noetherian-closedpoint-criterion; C:henselian-horizontal-proper; B:henselian-local-flat-proper; B:constant-integer-rigidity; B:nontorsion-rigidity; C:subject21-torsion-counterexample; B:H1-gate; C:torsion-degree-two-reduction; B:henselian; B:H0-counterexample; C:henselian-proper-closed-fibre; B:Fujiwara; B:henselized-affine-cover; B:henselized-Cech-obstruction; BHHW2024; BGabber1994; BFujiwara1995
notes: General qcqs H0 iff geometric henselianity. Unrestricted coefficients refuted on affine henselian pairs; general torsion implication now refuted by the full Nagata double construction for all constant Z/n,n>1. Positive affine/proper/affine-closed-fibre and separated finite-type noetherian henselian-base theorems retained. Distinct punctured comparison and HHW higher strengthening. Required original Gabber/Fujiwara theorem passages remain unavailable; modern complete proofs opened.

statement: Let $k$ be a field and $\mathcal C$ a rigid abelian $k$-linear symmetric tensor category with $\operatorname{End}(\mathbf1)=k$. If there is an exact faithful $k$-linear symmetric tensor functor $\omega:\mathcal C\to\operatorname{Vec}_k$, then \[ G=\operatorname{Aut}^{\otimes}(\omega) \] is an affine group scheme and $\mathcal C\simeq\operatorname{Rep}_k(G)$. Its other fibre functors over a $k$-algebra are classified by $G$-torsors. If such a fibre functor exists only after a field extension, the stack of fibre functors is an affine gerbe and its representation category recovers $\mathcal C$.
notes: Deligne–Milne corrected2022 edition2.11/3.2/3.9. Nonneutral theorem uses Deligne1990 correction; original1982 not silently credited with corrected theorem.

statement: If $\operatorname{char}k\ne2$, finite-dimensional super vector spaces with the Koszul symmetry form a rigid abelian symmetric tensor category with endomorphism ring $k$ of the unit, but admit no faithful symmetric tensor functor to ordinary vector spaces. Thus the sign and fibre-functor hypotheses cannot be removed from subject~22.
notes: Odd super line gives explicit obstruction to ordinary symmetric fibre functor; characteristic not2. Exact signs checked.

statement: For schemes of finite type over a field, ordinary Chow homology admits proper pushforward and flat pullback. If $Y$ is smooth quasi-projective of pure dimension $e$, $X$ is quasi-projective and pure of dimension $d$, and $f:X\to Y$ is any morphism, there is an integral pullback on classes \[ f^*: \mathrm{CH}^r(Y)\longrightarrow\mathrm{CH}_{d-r}(X), \qquad a\longmapsto f^*a\cap[X]. \] There is no smoothness assumption on $X$. For a separated regular noetherian scheme $Y$ of finite Krull dimension, rational Chow groups with supports have a canonical intersection product, agreeing with the Serre Tor formula when cycles meet properly. In particular $\mathrm{CH}^*(Y)_{\mathbb Q}$ is a graded commutative ring.
notes: Fulton integral smooth-quasiprojective target pullback; original GS1987Theorems8.2/8.3 rational supported product on separated regular noetherian finite-dimensional schemes. General integral regular-target assertion not proved here.

statement: Let $Y$ be a separated regular noetherian scheme of finite Krull dimension. Give it the dimension function $\delta_Y(y)=-\operatorname{codim}_Y(y)$, component by component, and give finite-type $Y$-schemes the induced dimension function. There is a canonical graded ring injection \[ \mathrm{CH}^*(Y)_{\mathbb Q}\longrightarrow A^*(Y)_{\mathbb Q}, \qquad \alpha\longmapsto\widetilde\alpha, \] into operational Chow cohomology, satisfying $\widetilde\alpha\cap[Y]=\alpha$. Consequently every morphism $f:X\to Y$ of finite type, with no regularity assumption on $X$, has canonical operations \[ f^*\widetilde\alpha\cap-: \mathrm{CH}_j(X)_{\mathbb Q}\longrightarrow \mathrm{CH}_{j-p}(X)_{\mathbb Q} \quad(\alpha\in\mathrm{CH}^p(Y)_{\mathbb Q}). \] They commute with proper pushforward, flat pullback and refined Cartier-divisor intersection, and are functorial under further pullback as operational classes. If $X$ is pure of dimension $d$ for the chosen dimension function, evaluating on $[X]$ gives a rational class in $\mathrm{CH}_{d-p}(X)$. Thus the regular-target assertion has an arbitrary-source rational form, including the ample-line-bundle setting of the manuscript.
notes: Complete reduction from Stacks42.58.1/42.56.6: unique K0 lift and Adams weights give canonical CH^p(Y)_Q→A^p(Y)_Q; pullback acts on Chow homology of arbitrary finite-type source X. All operation types/dimension grading explicit; no integral inference.

statement: Numerically trivial one-cycles on a smooth projective connected threefold need not be $\tau$-trivial. Numerical and rational-coefficient homological equivalence do agree for codimension-two cycles on every smooth projective fourfold in characteristic zero, and for abelian fourfolds in positive characteristic for every permitted $\ell$, using the 2026 Tate theorem stated in Theorem~\ref{B:abelian}.
depends_on: B:abelian; B:tau; B:betti; B:charzero; B:criterion; B:ancona-scope
notes: First question refuted; second proved for requested char0 and abelian classes; arbitrary positive-characteristic fourfold D is not declared solved.

statement: The product of two algebraically trivial cycles need not be rationally trivial, and an Albanese-trivial zero-cycle on a surface need not be rationally trivial. Both failures occur for the single explicit surface and cycles in Theorem~\ref{B:square}; the zero-cycle has infinite order. On a product of elliptic curves, the Albanese kernel is generated by the exterior products of degree-zero divisors.
notes: Both manuscript questions explicitly refuted by one integral construction; entire Albanese kernel generation supplied.

statement: Let $S$ be a scheme, $X\to S$ a smooth projective curve with geometrically connected fibres, and $D\subset X$ a relative effective Cartier divisor finite and faithfully flat over $S$. Put $D_n=V(\mathcal I_D^{n+1})$, and let $J_n$ be the relative Picard sheaf of the pinching $X\amalg_{D_n}S$, equivalently line bundles on $X$ trivialized along $D_n$. Let $J=\varprojlim_nJ_n$. The diagonal ideal supplies an Abel map $a:X\setminus D\to J$, and for every smooth commutative $S$-group scheme $G$, \[ \operatorname{Hom}_{S\text{-}\mathrm{grp}}(J,G) \xrightarrow{\ \circ a\ }\operatorname{Hom}_S(X\setminus D,G) \] is bijective. There is an exact sequence of fpqc sheaves \[ 1\longrightarrow\mathbb G_{m,S} \longrightarrow (D_n/S)_*\mathbb G_{m,D_n} \longrightarrow J_n\longrightarrow\operatorname{Pic}_{X/S} \longrightarrow1. \]
notes: Contou-Carrère2013§1.2(1.2.1–4), arbitrary-base relative Rosenlicht theorem, full Picard components retained. Original1990 chapter unavailable; full2013 primary restatement opened.

statement: For a noetherian scheme $X$ and a quasi-coherent sheaf $F$, the Parshin--Beilinson ad\`ele sheaves over flags give a functorial flasque resolution \[ 0\longrightarrow F\longrightarrow\mathcal A_X^0(F) \longrightarrow\mathcal A_X^1(F)\longrightarrow\cdots. \] Its global-sections complex computes $R\Gamma(X,F)$. For a noetherian ring $A$, a formal curve $\mathfrak X=\operatorname{Spf}B$ with $B\simeq A[[t]]$, and $U=\operatorname{Spec}B[1/t]$, define the local Jacobian as the Zariski group sheaf with \[ \mathcal J(R)=\bigl(R[[t]][t^{-1}]\bigr)^\times \qquad(R\text{ an }A\text{-algebra}). \] There is an Abel map $a:U\to\mathcal J_{\mathrm{omb}}$ to its formal shadow such that, for every smooth separated commutative $A$-group scheme $G$, \[ \operatorname{Hom}_{A\text{-}\mathrm{grp}}(\mathcal J,G) \xrightarrow{\ h\mapsto h_{\mathrm{omb}}\circ a\ }G(U) \quad\text{is bijective}. \]
notes: BGW2016Theorems2.1/4.17; CC2013Theorems1.4.4/1.6.6 with noetherian base and formal-shadow Abel map. Huber original proof of adèle resolution not separately opened.

statement: For finite-type schemes over $\mathbb Z$ there are the triangulated categories of rational Beilinson motives $\mathrm{DM}_{\mathrm B}(X)$ and their constructible subcategories. For separated finite-type morphisms the six operations preserve constructibility. If $a:X\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb Z$ is separated of finite type, then $a^!\mathbf1$ is dualizing on constructible motives: with \[ D_X(M)=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(M,a^!\mathbf1) \] the canonical map $M\to D_XD_XM$ is an isomorphism, and duality exchanges the expected pairs of six operations.
notes: Cisinski–Déglise15.2.1/15.2.4 rational constructible triangulated six-operations and duality over arithmetic bases. Does not assert unconditional abelian mixed-motive category.

statement: Every generically reduced noetherian quasi-excellent scheme $X$ over $\mathbb Q$ admits a finite sequence of blowups along regular centres, all disjoint from the inverse image of $X_{\mathrm{reg}}$, whose final scheme is regular. The sequence can be chosen functorially for regular morphisms, omitting empty blowups after base change. For a noetherian quasi-excellent scheme $X$, a nowhere dense closed subset $Z$, and a prime $\ell$ invertible on $X$, there is a finite family $\{X_i\to X\}$ covering in the $\ell'$-alteration topology such that each $X_i$ is regular and integral and the inverse image of $Z$ is the support of a strict normal-crossings divisor. This latter assertion does not assert a birational resolution in positive characteristic.
notes: Temkin2012Theorem1.2.1 characteristic0 and Gabber ℓ′-alteration uniformization ILOIX1.1; latter permits field alterations, not general birational resolution.

statement: Let $n\geq1$ be invertible on a noetherian regular scheme $X$, and let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed regular subscheme of pure codimension $c$. With $\Lambda=\mathbb Z/n\mathbb Z$, the cycle-class Gysin map is an isomorphism \[ \Lambda_Z(-c)[-2c]\xrightarrow{\sim}i^!\Lambda_X. \] Consequently $R^qi^!\Lambda_X=0$ for $q\ne2c$, and $R^{2c}i^!\Lambda_X=\Lambda_Z(-c)$.
notes: ILO XVI3.1.1: regular noetherian ambient and closed scheme; n invertible; codimensionc twist and shift verified.

statement: Let $f:Y\to X$ be a regular morphism of locally noetherian $\mathbb Z[1/n]$-schemes, let $g:X'\to X$ be quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and form $Y'=Y\times_XX'$ with projections $g':Y'\to Y$ and $f':Y'\to X'$. For every $K\in D^+(X'_{\acute et},\mathbb Z/n\mathbb Z)$ the canonical map \[ f^*Rg_*K\xrightarrow{\sim}Rg'_*f'^*K \] is an isomorphism. In particular this applies to the completion map of an excellent noetherian local ring.
notes: ILO XIV2.5.3/XVII4.2.1: regular locally noetherian base change, qcqs other map, bounded-below complexes; completion application requires excellence.

statement: Let $X$ be an excellent noetherian $\mathbb Z[1/n]$-scheme with a dimension function $\delta$, and put $\Lambda=\mathbb Z/n\mathbb Z$. There is a potential dualizing complex $K_{X,\delta}$, uniquely determined together with its compatible local normalizations. It belongs to $D^b_{ctf}(X_{\acute et},\Lambda)$, and \[ D_X(M)=R\mathcal Hom_\Lambda(M,K_{X,\delta}) \] preserves $D^b_c(X_{\acute et},\Lambda)$. For every $M$ in that category, $M\to D_XD_X(M)$ is an isomorphism. If $X$ has finite Krull dimension, $K_{X,\delta}$ has finite quasi-injective dimension and is a dualizing complex in the sense of SGA~5.
notes: ILO XVII5.1.1/6.1.1: excellent noetherian, dimension function, torsion invertible, local normalizations; biduality all Db_c, K in Db_ctf.

statement: Let $X$ be noetherian and quasi-excellent, let $f:Y\to X$ be of finite type, and let $n$ be invertible on $X$. For a constructible $\mathbb Z/n\mathbb Z$-sheaf $F$ on $Y_{\acute et}$, every $R^qf_*F$ is constructible and these sheaves vanish for all sufficiently large $q$. Thus $Rf_*$ preserves bounded constructible complexes. Without invertibility, even finiteness of $H^1$ over an algebraically closed field can fail.
notes: ILO XIII1.1.1 constructibility and boundedness; explicit Artin–Schreier polynomial proof of failure without invertibility.

statement: Let $X$ be a quasi-excellent scheme equipped with a dimension function $\delta_X$, let $n$ be invertible on $X$, let $f:Y\to X$ be affine of finite type, and let $F$ be a constructible $\mathbb Z/n\mathbb Z$-sheaf on $Y$. Put \[ \delta_Y(y)=\delta_X(f(y))+operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(y))}\kappa(y), \qquad \delta_X(G)=\sup_{G_{\bar x}\ne0}\delta_X(x). \] Then $\delta_X(R^qf_*F)\leq\delta_Y(F)-q$. In particular, for an affine $d$-dimensional scheme of finite type over an algebraically closed field, cohomology with constructible prime-to-characteristic torsion coefficients vanishes above degree $d$.
notes: ILO XV1.1.2 relative support-sensitive affine Lefschetz dimension inequality and absolute bound derived.

statement: For a proper holomorphic map $f:X\to S$ of complex spaces and a coherent analytic sheaf $F$ on $X$, every $R^qf_*F$ is coherent. In particular $H^q(X,F)$ is finite dimensional when $X$ is compact. This does not, without further hypotheses, say that $R^qf_*F$ is locally free or that arbitrary base change commutes with it.
notes: Grauert1960§6HauptsatzI,p59: proper holomorphic coherent direct image; finite-dimensional compact consequence; no extra base-change/local-freeness claim.

statement: Let $K$ be a complete algebraically closed nonarchimedean field with a nontrivial valuation, and let $A$ be a classical $K$-affinoid algebra of dimension $d$. For every torsion abelian sheaf $F$ on $(\operatorname{Spec}A)_{\acute et}$, \[ H^i(\operatorname{Spec}A,F)=0\quad(i>d+1). \] If $F$ is $\ell$-primary and $\ell$ is different from the residue characteristic of $K$, the stronger bound is $i>d$.
notes: Bhatt–Mathew7.3: classical affinoid over complete algebraically closed nontrivially valued field; algebraic étale site specified, d+1 all torsion and d prime-to-residue characteristic.
