statement: Let $(X,Y)$ be a Hausdorff polyhedral pair, meaning a pair homeomorphic to a locally finite simplicial complex and a subcomplex, with $X$ second countable. Let $n\geq1$. Suppose every $y\in Y$ has a fundamental system of neighbourhoods $U$ for which $(U,U\setminus Y)$ is $(n-1)$-connected. Then $(X,X\setminus Y)$ is $(n-1)$-connected. The implication therefore applies to second-countable finite-dimensional complex analytic spaces and closed analytic subspaces whenever the stated local depth bound holds.
notes: Identifies actual SGA2(1962); Eyral2000Theorem2.4 and full proof opened. Independent finite-polyhedral ConjectureA refutation and exact conical repair in B:local-Hurewicz. HL1990 locators from opened SGA annotations, full chapter not opened or used as a proof input.

statement: There is a finite polyhedral pair $(X,Y)$, with $Y$ a single point $v$, such that \[ \mathcal H^i_Y(\mathbb Z_X)=0\quad(i<4),\qquad \pi_2^Y(X,v)=0,\qquad \pi_3^Y(X,v)=\mathbb Z/2. \] It refutes SGA~2, Expos\'e XIII, \S6, Conjecture A, which is stated for topological locally triangulable pairs and includes the local fundamental-group condition. For an arbitrary nonempty connected finite polyhedron $L$, let $X=cL$ be its cone and $Y=\{v\}$ its vertex. For every $n\geq3$, the exact replacement is \[ \operatorname{prof\,hpt}_{Y}(X)\geq n \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \begin{cases} \pi_1(L)=0,\\ \widetilde H^j(L,\mathbb Z)=0& (j<n-1),\\ H^{n-1}(L,\mathbb Z)\text{ is torsion-free}. \end{cases} \] The last condition is equivalently torsion-freeness of $\mathcal H^n_Y(\mathbb Z_X)_v$.
notes: Original ConjectureA explicitly topological with locally triangulable pairs. Complete finite-polyhedral counterexample: cone on suspension of ten-face six-vertex complex, integral H2(link)=Z/2, local cohomology vanishes below4 but local pi3 nonzero. All faces/boundaries/SNF checked. Exact finite-conical iff correction adds torsion-free next cohomology; proof via UCT and Hurewicz, n3 separately handled.

statement: Let $R$ be a complete discrete valuation ring with fraction field $K$, uniformizer $\pi$, and perfect residue field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$. Equal and mixed characteristic are both allowed. Fix a coefficient map $W(k)\to R$. For a finite product $L$ of perfect field extensions of $k$, put \[ R(L)=\varprojlim_n \bigl(W_n(L)\otimes_{W_n(k)}R/\mathfrak m_R^n\bigr), \qquad K(L)=R(L)[1/\pi]. \] For $R=k[[t]]$ with its specified coefficient field, these are $L[[t]]$ and $L((t))$. For $L$ a field, $R(L)$ is a complete discrete valuation ring with residue field $L$. Let $S_{\mathrm{pa}}$ be the étale site on finite products of perfect field extensions of $k$, $S_{\mathrm{pf}}$ the pro-fppf site on quasi-compact quasi-separated perfect $k$-schemes, and $S_{\mathrm{ir}}$ the pro-étale site on ind-rational $k$-algebras. Here rational algebras are finite products of perfections of finitely generated field extensions, and ind-rational algebras are filtered unions of rational subalgebras. In the pro-fppf site, coverings are finite jointly surjective families flat of profinite presentation in the perfect sense. The inclusions induce premorphisms \[ h:S_{\mathrm{pf}}\to S_{\mathrm{pa}},\qquad \widetilde h:S_{\mathrm{pf}}\to S_{\mathrm{ir}},\qquad \mathsf a=R\widetilde h_*Lh^*: D(S_{\mathrm{pa}},\mathbf{Ab})\to D(S_{\mathrm{ir}},\mathbf{Ab}). \] These premorphisms are not assumed to have exact inverse image on arbitrary sheaves of sets. \begin{enumerate} \item Let $\mathcal P'_{\mathrm{fc}}$ consist of commutative proalgebraic groups representable as extensions of perfections of abelian varieties by perfect affine groups, with finite étale component group. Restriction to $S_{\mathrm{pa}}$ is fully faithful on this category, and its derived counit is an isomorphism: \[ Lh^*(P|_{S_{\mathrm{pa}}})\simeq P \quad\text{in }D(S_{\mathrm{pf}},\mathbf{Ab}). \] \item The functors $R(-),K(-)$ induce premorphisms $\pi_R:R_{\mathrm{fppf}}\to S_{\mathrm{pa}}$ and $\pi_K:K_{\mathrm{fppf}}\to S_{\mathrm{pa}}$. Define \[ \mathcal R_R(F)=\mathsf aR\pi_{R,*}F,\qquad \mathcal R_K(F)=\mathsf aR\pi_{K,*}F,\qquad \mathcal R_x(F)= \operatorname{fib}\bigl(\mathcal R_R(F)\to\mathcal R_K(F|_K)\bigr). \] They give a functorial localization triangle. Call $Q\in D(S_{\mathrm{pa}},\mathbf{Ab})$ $h$-acyclic if its unit $Q\to Rh_*Lh^*Q$ is an isomorphism. If $R\pi_{R,*}F$ is $h$-acyclic, then \[ R\Gamma(L_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},\mathcal R_R(F)) \simeq R\Gamma(R(L)_{\mathrm{fppf}},F). \] The analogous assertion holds over $K$. If both unit conditions hold for $F$ and $F|_K$, the analogous comparison holds with support on the closed fibre. Under this unit hypothesis, if both $F$ and $\mathcal R_R(F)$ are bounded below, there is the spectral sequence \[ E_2^{ij}= H^i(L_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},\mathcal H^j\mathcal R_R(F)) \Longrightarrow H^{i+j}(R(L)_{\mathrm{fppf}},F). \] For algebraically closed $L$, this reduces to $\mathcal H^q\mathcal R_R(F)(L)=H^q(R(L)_{\mathrm{fppf}},F)$. \item If $G/R$ is a smooth commutative group scheme of finite type, write $G_n=G\times_RR/\mathfrak m_R^n$ and \[ \mathbf G=\varprojlim_n \bigl(\operatorname{Gr}_{R/\mathfrak m_R^n}(G_n)\bigr)^{\mathrm{perf}}. \] Then $\mathbf G\in\mathcal P'_{\mathrm{fc}}$ and \[ 0\longrightarrow U_G\longrightarrow\mathbf G \longrightarrow G_k^{\mathrm{perf}}\longrightarrow0 \] is exact, with $U_G$ connected pro-unipotent. Consequently $\pi_0(\mathbf G)=\pi_0(G_k)$, and $\mathcal R_R(G)\simeq\mathbf G[0]$. The unit condition in the preceding clause holds. \item If $N/R$ is finite flat and commutative, then $\mathcal H^0\mathcal R_R(N)$ is finite étale and agrees with $\mathcal H^0\mathcal R_K(N_K)$, $\mathcal H^1\mathcal R_R(N)$ is connected pro-unipotent, and $\mathcal H^q\mathcal R_R(N)=0$ for $q\geq2$. The object $R\pi_{R,*}N$ is $h$-acyclic. \end{enumerate}
notes: Strongest scoped modern theorem for subject11: complete DVR, perfect positive-characteristic residue field, precise perfect/pro-fppf/ind-rational sites, derived counit and separately retained unit acyclicity, bounded-below relative output for convergence, smooth and finite-flat coefficient calculations. Full primary proof audits by B/C; root independently checked the exact statements, derived typing, cited Sections7--8/10 and the complete used Suzuki2018/Begueri proofs. No exact historical-site identity or unrestricted injective-preservation claim.

statement: Let $X$ be a separated finite-type $R_m$-scheme, not necessarily reduced. Its finite Greenberg realization $\operatorname{Gr}_m(X)$ is a separated finite-type $k$-scheme characterized by \[ \operatorname{Gr}_m(X)(A)=X(R_m\otimes_k A) \] for every $k$-algebra $A$. Define the finite-partition presheaf by \[ N_m(X)(Y)=\varinjlim_P\prod_{S\in P} X\bigl(R_m\otimes_k\Gamma(S,\mathcal O_S)\bigr). \] There are natural bijections \[ \begin{aligned} N_m(X)(Y) &\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_k\bigl(T(Y),\operatorname{Gr}_m(X)\bigr)\\ &\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Abs}_k} \bigl(T(Y),T(\operatorname{Gr}_m(X))\bigr). \end{aligned} \] In particular this is a realization of the finite-partition construction in the absolutely flat category, using its internal products. The Greenberg functor preserves products and group objects.
notes: Equal-characteristic finite truncation; algebraically closed k; separated finite-type X, possibly nonreduced; finite reduced test partitions. Exact realization in the absolutely flat category and product/group preservation proved.

statement: Put $R=k[[t]]$, $A=k[x]$, and let $P$ range over the same finite reduced affine locally closed partitions of $\operatorname{Spec}A$. The natural homomorphism \[ D:=\varinjlim_P A_P[[t]]\longrightarrow T(A)[[t]] \] is injective but not surjective. Nevertheless, for every $m\geq1$, \[ D/t^mD\simeq T(A)[t]/(t^m),\qquad \widehat D^{\,(t)}\simeq T(A)[[t]]. \] In particular $D$ is a proper dense subring of its $t$-adic completion, and \[ \varinjlim_P\varprojlim_m A_P[t]/(t^m) \;\longrightarrow\; \varprojlim_m\varinjlim_P A_P[t]/(t^m) \] is not surjective. This is already the additive-group construction for $\mathbb G_{a,R}$; it is not caused by singularities or non-affineness.
notes: Explicit singleton-idempotent series refutes an infinite-limit/finite-partition interchange. Injectivity, every truncated quotient and proper dense completion are proved. Infinite argument, not a finite-computation claim.

statement: Let $k$ be algebraically closed. On the category of reduced affine finite-type $k$-schemes, equip fibre products with their reduced scheme structures and take finite surjective morphisms as covers. For $Y=\operatorname{Spec}B$ define the presheaves of additive abelian groups \[ D(Y)=\varinjlim_P B_P[[t]],\qquad E(Y)=T(B)[[t]], \] where $P$ runs over finite affine locally closed reduced partitions of $Y$. The induced morphism of associated \emph{sheaves of abelian groups} \[ D^\#\longrightarrow E^\# \] is not an epimorphism. The same is true for the associated sheaves of sets. In particular the series $z$ of Proposition~\ref{B:uniform-partition-obstruction} has no local lift from $D^\#$ on this specified site. No conclusion about categorical epimorphisms of sheaves of rings is asserted.
notes: Obstruction persists under every finite surjective cover of the specified reduced affine finite-type site, hence after sheafification in sets or additive abelian groups. No assertion about ring epimorphisms or the entire historical site.

statement: Let $R$ be a complete discrete valuation ring with perfect residue field $k$ and uniformizer $\pi$. In equal characteristic fix an isomorphism $R\simeq k[[t]]$ carrying $\pi$ to $t$. In mixed characteristic use the canonical Cohen inclusion $W(k)\hookrightarrow R$. Put $R_n=R/(\pi^n)$ and let $\mathcal R_n$ be its finite Greenberg ring scheme over $k$. For a $k$-algebra $A$, assume that $A$ is perfect in mixed characteristic, and define \[ S(A)=\varprojlim_n\mathcal R_n(A). \] For every $R$-scheme $X$, without a finite-type or separatedness assumption, the scheme \[ \operatorname{Gr}_R(X)= \varprojlim_n\operatorname{Gr}_{R_n}(X\times_R R_n) \] exists. There are natural bijections \[ \operatorname{Gr}_R(X)(A) \simeq\varprojlim_n X\bigl(\mathcal R_n(A)\bigr) \simeq X\bigl(S(A)\bigr), \] where all points on the right are morphisms over $R$. Here \[ S(A)\simeq \begin{cases} A[[t]],&R\simeq k[[t]],\\ R\otimes_{W(k)}W(A),&\operatorname{char}R=0,\ \operatorname{char}k>0. \end{cases} \] The construction preserves products and group objects. It is generally not of finite type: for $X=\mathbb A^1_R$ its underlying scheme is $\operatorname{Spec}k[x_0,x_1,\ldots]$.
notes: Arbitrary R-scheme; complete DVR with perfect residue field, perfect test algebra in mixed characteristic. Explicit derivation from corrected BGA17.5/18.2 and Bhatt2014Theorem4.1/Remark4.6; completeness and relative typing checked; no finite-partition interchange.

statement: Use standard $p$-typical Witt coordinates and write $[f]=(f,0,0,\ldots)$. For every commutative ring $A$, every $f\in A$, every $N\geq0$, and every $w=(w_i)_{i\geq0}\in W(A)$, one has \[ ([f]^Nw)_i=f^{Np^i}w_i. \tag{\(*\)} \] Consequently, for $A=\mathbb F_p[f]$, with $f$ an indeterminate, the canonical map \[ W(A)_{[f]}\longrightarrow W(A_f) \] is injective and is not surjective. An explicit element outside its image has coordinates $v_i=f^{-ip^i}$. The same conclusions and witness hold for the perfect domain $A=\mathbb F_p[f^{1/p^r}:r\geq0]$. In contrast, the vector with coordinates $w_i=f^{-i}$ does lie in $W(A)_{[f]}$. Thus this particular illustrative vector in \cite[Remark~18.3]{BBertapelleGonzalezAviles2022} must be replaced when using the standard-coordinate convention explicitly fixed in that source, Section~2.3, pp.~8--9. The localization inequality and the corrected Greenberg theorem remain valid.
notes: Universal ghost-polynomial identity; corrected explicit nonlocalizable vector in polynomial/perfect domains. Source coordinate convention checked; original illustrative tuple belongs to the localization. Existing147-check certificate supplements the full infinite proof.
